Orig Code / Protocol: Original MATLAB repo (zzhiwu/SPDNet) loads pre-computed .mat covariance descriptors on a single fixed random split without temporal filtering or BatchNorm, and reports peak test-set accuracy over epochs.

Our spd_learn Fix: Normalized SPDNet in spd_learn with orthogonal trivialization (BiMap), ReEig(1e-4), and trace-scaled shrinkage. On Voyager, SPDNet reaches 58.01±0.1458.01 \pm 0.1458.01±0.14% on HDM05, 96.96±0.4896.96 \pm 0.4896.96±0.48% on 40×4040\times 4040×40 Radar, 90.26±0.4190.26 \pm 0.4190.26±0.41% on FPHA, 28.36±2.1528.36 \pm 2.1528.36±2.15% on AFEW, and 62.81±16.5062.81 \pm 16.5062.81±16.50% on BNCI2014-001.

BNCI2014-001 BNCI2015-001 Lee2019 Hinss2021

Domain-Specific Momentum Batch Normalization Closes the Cross-Session EEG Transfer Gap by 8.33 Percentage Points

BNCI2014-001: Pub 74.60±11.2074.60 \pm 11.2074.60±11.20% vs. Ours 63.31±11.6863.31 \pm 11.6863.31±11.68%

✓ 2 Verified ◐ 1 Baseline-Adjusted Inspect Figures, 4 Tables & Gap →
! Author Transductive Test-Session Leakage (-11.29% Causal Δ) -11.29% BNCI-001

Orig Code / Protocol: HUMAN / PROTOCOL ERROR: Original rkobler/TSMNet computes **transductive domain-specific batch normalization (SPDDSMBN)** over the **entire unlabeled test session (1test) simultaneously**. This leaks the target session's Riemannian Fréchet mean and dispersion across all 288 test trials before making a single prediction.

Our spd_learn Fix: Under strictly **causal inductive zero-shot evaluation** (eval() using frozen source-session running stats) on Voyager BNCI2014-001, TSMNet drops from 74.60% (transductive) to **63.31±11.6863.31 \pm 11.6863.31±11.68%** (best checkpoint) and **60.03±11.9560.03 \pm 11.9560.03±11.95%** (final epoch, +3.28% test-peeking gap).

Original Authors' Code / Protocol Root Cause

Original paper evaluates 2-class Left/Right Hand ROC-AUC on C=3C=3C=3 channels (C3, Cz, C4) under 5-fold Within-Session CV (Table 2). Applying large delay embedding m≥5m \ge 5m≥5 naively to C=22C=22C=22 or C=62C=62C=62 channels produces (mC)×(mC)(mC) \times (mC)(mC)×(mC) matrices that are strictly rank-deficient (rank⁡≤T<mC\operatorname{rank} \le T < mCrank≤T<mC).

Our spd_learn Code / Harness Fix

Matched both the native 3-channel (C3, Cz, C4) Within-Session ROC-AUC protocol (within -0.34% across 6 datasets) and scaled delay embedding to m=2,τ=1m=2, \tau=1m=2,τ=1 (44×4444 \times 4444×44 SPD) for multi-channel Cross-Session decoding, achieving **69.13±14.3869.13 \pm 14.3869.13±14.38%** (final 68.79%) on BNCI2014-001 (#2 of 24 models!) and **69.55%** 10-dataset mean (#3 of 24 models).

Dataloader & Preprocessing Diff

Original paper uses 3 channels (C3, Cz, C4) in [8-32] Hz with 5-fold Within-Session CV (ROC-AUC); Voyager also evaluates full-montage 4-class Cross-Session (0train →\to→ 1test).

Where It Fails / Boundary Regime

When m⋅C>Tm \cdot C > Tm⋅C>T (e.g. m=6m=6m=6 on C=62C=62C=62 channels = 372×372372 \times 372372×372 covariance from T=384T=384T=384 samples), sample covariances become rank-deficient without spatial pre-reduction.

Original Authors' Code / Protocol Root Cause

In Roche/neuro-green, default Gabor wavelet parameters oct_min=0, oct_max=3 span [20,23]=[1,8] Hz[2^0, 2^3] = [1, 8]\text{ Hz}[20,23]=[1,8] Hz (delta/theta resting-state bands for brain-age regression) and the authors' pipeline relies on custom MNE-BIDS + autoreject bad-epoch/channel cleaning. On motor imagery ([8, 30] Hz), oct_min=0..3 puts 75% of wavelets below 8 Hz8\text{ Hz}8 Hz.

Our spd_learn Code / Harness Fix

Repaired Green wavelet bounds to [4,32] Hz[4, 32]\text{ Hz}[4,32] Hz (oct_min=2.0, oct_max=5.0), lifting BNCI2014-001 from 53.20% ([1,8] Hz) to **68.48±14.6468.48 \pm 14.6468.48±14.64%** (85.83% on S1), BNCI2014-004 to **79.44±10.6779.44 \pm 10.6779.44±10.67%**, LEMON to **70.83±16.5470.83 \pm 16.5470.83±16.54%**, and uncleaned TUAB to **61.09±3.1261.09 \pm 3.1261.09±3.12%** (-24.01% vs autoreject), achieving the **#2 highest 10-dataset MOABB mean (70.16%)** across all 24 SPD models!

Dataloader & Where It Struggles

Original GREEN repo uses MNE-BIDS + autoreject automated bad-epoch/channel cleaning on clinical EEG (TUAB: 85.10% with autoreject vs 61.09% uncleaned on Voyager; LEMON: 70.83%); Voyager runs uncleaned clinical and MOABB epochs without autoreject. Without autoreject trial cleaning, severe clinical/ocular artifacts on uncleaned TUAB (61.09% vs 85.10% published) and noisy MI subjects (BNCI2014-001 S2: 47.57%) lower accuracy.

3 · THE GAP & WHY -11.29% BNCI-001
Original Authors' Code / Protocol Root Cause

HUMAN / PROTOCOL ERROR: Original rkobler/TSMNet computes **transductive domain-specific batch normalization (SPDDSMBN)** over the **entire unlabeled test session (1test) simultaneously**. This leaks the target session's Riemannian Fréchet mean and dispersion across all 288 test trials before making a single prediction.

Our spd_learn Code / Harness Fix

Under strictly **causal inductive zero-shot evaluation** (eval() using frozen source-session running stats) on Voyager BNCI2014-001, TSMNet drops from 74.60% (transductive) to **63.31±11.6863.31 \pm 11.6863.31±11.68%** (best checkpoint) and **60.03±11.9560.03 \pm 11.9560.03±11.95%** (final epoch, +3.28% test-peeking gap).

Dataloader & Preprocessing Diff

Paper evaluates transductive target-session batch normalization across the whole test session and drops Fpz on Hinss2021; Voyager evaluates causal single-trial zero-shot inference (0train →\to→ 1test) without access to future test trials.

Where It Fails / Boundary Regime

Collapses in causal online BCI (batch_size=1, 60.03% final-epoch mean on BNCI2014-001; S2: 47.22%, S6: 50.00%) where target-session Fréchet statistics are unavailable.

Original Authors' Code / Protocol Root Cause

Original MATLAB repo (zzhiwu/SPDNet) loads pre-computed .mat covariance descriptors on a single fixed random split without temporal filtering or BatchNorm, and reports peak test-set accuracy over epochs.

Our spd_learn Code / Harness Fix

Normalized SPDNet in spd_learn with orthogonal trivialization (BiMap), ReEig(1e-4), and trace-scaled shrinkage. On Voyager, SPDNet reaches 58.01±0.1458.01 \pm 0.1458.01±0.14% on HDM05, 96.96±0.4896.96 \pm 0.4896.96±0.48% on 40×4040\times 4040×40 Radar, 90.26±0.4190.26 \pm 0.4190.26±0.41% on FPHA, 28.36±2.1528.36 \pm 2.1528.36±2.15% on AFEW, and 62.81±16.5062.81 \pm 16.5062.81±16.50% on BNCI2014-001.

Dataloader & Where It Struggles

Paper loads pre-computed MATLAB .mat descriptors on a single fixed split; Voyager recomputes sample covariances across HDM05, Radar, FPHA, AFEW, and 9 BNCI2014-001 CrossSession subjects. Without temporal convolutions or Riemannian BatchNorm, SPDNet suffers severe cross-session drift on low-SNR EEG subjects (BNCI2014-001 S2: 47.57%, S6: 41.67%) and 400×400400 \times 400400×400 AFEW (28.36%).

3 · THE GAP & WHY -0.83% vs Tuned SPDNet
Original Authors' Code / Protocol Root Cause

THREE AUTHOR FLAWS in GitZH-Chen/LieBN: (1) Claims +8.8% to +3.6% gains on HDM05 by comparing against an under-trained SPDNet (59.13%) / SPDNetBN (65.24%); (2) Uses a single-step (n_iter=1) Karcher approximation for AIM LieBN that leaves a **51.3 Frobenius centering residual** at κ≈1.9×107\kappa \approx 1.9 \times 10^7κ≈1.9×107; (3) On FPHA (where 454/1,175 raw trials are rank-deficient with T<63T < 63T<63), LieBN-LCM drops to 78.19% (-12.07% below Table 4c's 90.26% claim).

Our spd_learn Code / Harness Fix

On Voyager HDM05 (identical 60-ep cosine schedule), LieBN-AIM (70.85±1.1770.85 \pm 1.1770.85±1.17%), LieBN-LEM (70.69±1.6870.69 \pm 1.6870.69±1.68%), and LieBN-LCM (70.15±0.3970.15 \pm 0.3970.15±0.39%) do **not** beat properly tuned 2019 SPDNetBN (**71.68±1.5171.68 \pm 1.5171.68±1.51%**), while LieBN-AIM reaches 92.00±0.4392.00 \pm 0.4392.00±0.43% on shrinkage-repaired FPHA and 97.39±0.5897.39 \pm 0.5897.39±0.58% on 40×4040\times 4040×40 Radar.

Dataloader & Preprocessing Diff

Paper compares against under-tuned baseline numbers copied from older papers on a single split; Voyager trains SPDNetBN and all 3 LieBN metrics under identical splits across HDM05, Radar, FPHA, and AFEW.

Where It Fails / Boundary Regime

C2 & C3 Falsified: 1-step AIM Karcher fails to center ill-conditioned matrices (51.3 error), LieBN-LCM drops -12.07% on FPHA (78.19% vs 90.26%), and all 3 LieBN variants (70.15%–70.85%) trail tuned SPDNetBN (71.68%) on HDM05.

Original Authors' Code / Protocol Root Cause

TWO AUTHOR FLAWS: (1) Normalizing patch covariances to correlation matrices C++n\mathcal{C}_{++}^nC++n​ (D−1/2ΣD−1/2D^{-1/2} \Sigma D^{-1/2}D−1/2ΣD−1/2) forces all diagonal entries to 111, **erasing per-channel log-bandpower (ERD/ERS variance)**; (2) Reported 75.80% relies on per-epoch test-set checkpoint peeking.

Our spd_learn Code / Harness Fix

Implemented CorAtt (cov_to_corr + corr_olm_log / corr_lsm_log) in spd_learn. Under our causal 40-epoch Voyager harness, CorAtt reaches **65.59±13.1865.59 \pm 13.1865.59±13.18%** (final 65.05%, -10.21% below published 75.80%) on BNCI2014-001 and **79.25±10.6779.25 \pm 10.6779.25±10.67%** on BNCI2014-004.

Dataloader & Preprocessing Diff

Authors' training loop selects best test accuracy across epochs; Voyager evaluates standardized 40-epoch MOABB CrossSession splits.

Where It Fails / Boundary Regime

Erasing diagonal channel variances (D=diag⁡(Σ)D = \operatorname{diag}(\Sigma)D=diag(Σ)) discards sensorimotor mu/beta power desynchronization, costing -3.97% vs GraphCSPNet (69.56%) on BNCI2014-001.

CLAIM 1D-1 · LOW-CHANNEL REGIME (d≤19d \le 19d≤19)7 Datasets

To test whether scale-invariant correlation projection preserves discriminative power on sparse sensor montages, we compared all 6 families on the 7 low-dimensional datasets (d∈[2,19]d \in [2, 19]d∈[2,19], tangent dimension 3–1903\text{--}1903–190). Correlation models drop to 56.88% (-5.25% below Riemannian BatchNorm at 62.13%), confirming that projecting P↦Δ(P)−1/2PΔ(P)−1/2P \mapsto \Delta(P)^{-1/2}P\Delta(P)^{-1/2}P↦Δ(P)−1/2PΔ(P)−1/2 discards up to half of the degrees of freedom when diagonal log-variance carries the primary ERD/ERS signal.

CLAIM 1D-2 · HIGH-DENSITY EEG (d∈[56,64]d \in [56, 64]d∈[56,64])11 Datasets

To determine when spatial filterbanks outperform metric normalization, we evaluated the 11 high-density cohorts (56–6456\text{--}6456–64 channels, tangent dimension 1,596–2,0801,596\text{--}2,0801,596–2,080). Foundational spatiotemporal filterbanks (TSMNet, EEGSPDNet, Green, TensorCSPNet) rise to #1 across all families at 64.45% (ahead of BatchNorm at 63.61%), suggesting that dense 60+ electrode montages provide the spatial resolution needed to isolate focal cortical sources prior to covariance pooling.
